prerequisites: Basic training modules (common to industrial branch and electrical specific technology)
Solid knowledge in Electrical Technology, Circuit Theory and Electrical Networks, Transmission and Distribution of Electrical Energy, and Electrical Power Plants and Systems
Having taken or currently taking 'Management and Operation of Electrical Energy Systems'

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the concept of Microgrid and establish the differences and similarities with conventional power grids, their advantages, disadvantages, and potential (RMR-1).
Understand the concept of Distributed Generation and the analogies and differences this concept presents with respect to centralized generation.

Know and recognize the different generating and energy storage sources susceptible to being installed in a microgrid, their operation, particularities, and main applications in the field of microgrids (RMR-2).
Analyze the needs of the connection interface depending on the type of generator and type of microgrid to which it is connected, and design said interface (RMR-3).

Select the most appropriate management philosophy for each type of microgrid based on the specifications, generators, and storage sources inserted in it, and simulate the behavior of the microgrid with the selected philosophy (RMR-4).
Know and apply the recommendations and regulations applicable in the field of electrical microgrids (RME-5).

syllabus_topics: The concept of microgrids and distributed generation.
Integration of renewables into the electrical system.
EU Regulation 2016/631 and technical supervision standard.
teaching_methods: Laboratory / field / computer lab / language lab practices
assessment_rules: For ordinary examination, if all minimums for the theoretical block are met, the final grade is calculated as 0.7 * (Average of T1) + 0.3 * P1. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. Partial exams with a score below 4 are considered failed and can be retaken in the official call. For extraordinary examination, a theoretical exam and a practical exam are conducted. To pass, a minimum of 4.5 points out of 10 is required in both the theoretical and practical parts. If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as (0.7 * Theory) + (0.3 * Practices); otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. In case of doubt regarding authorship or unauthorized means, an in-person defense may be requested.
bibliography: S. Chowdhury, “Microgrids and Active Distribution Networks”, IET, 2009.
